rationale: This is a straight linear blend of two already-evaluated archive signals (IndustryWCAccrualGrossProfit and WorkingCapitalBloatVsPeers) using the same inputs and same aggregation operator, so it will almost mechanically land between their existing statistics rather than test a new economic mechanism.

A one-term extension of the archived WeakestLinkCashQuality using the same three legs already in the archive is a cosmetic variant, and since the two-way MIN already underperformed the additive version on both fmb_tstat and alpha, adding a third binding constraint predictably narrows the extremes and degrades stability rather than resolving anything.

Gating accruals on sales growth is economically the correct scaler and genuinely distinct from the profitability and leverage gates already tested, though the reviewer should note it is a crude cousin of the (modified) Jones-model idea that accruals are only abnormal net of revenue growth, and the RANK multiplier mutes the signal for high-growth firms in a way that must be checked against a simple growth tilt.

Swapping the profitability level for a one-year margin change is a substantively different and internally consistent construction, but it overlaps materially with the Abarbanell-Bushee/Piotroski fundamental-signal literature and discards the gross-profitability anchor that carries essentially all the alpha in the archive, so the likely outcome is a weaker rather than complementary result.

Deleting the current-liability term from the archive's generation-0 leader is a minimal edit, and the asset-side-versus-liability-side decomposition of accruals is well-trodden published ground (Thomas and Zhang on inventory as the driver of the accrual anomaly), so the informational content is largely a known decomposition of an already-evaluated signal.

Retained-earnings-to-assets is a genuinely different, longer-horizon quality dimension than the contemporaneous margins and short-window ROE volatility used everywhere else in the archive, and the construction matches the hypothesis cleanly; the main caveat is that RE/AT is heavily loaded on firm maturity and distress (Altman-Z style), so the result should be checked against a simple maturity or distress tilt.
